crime: Corporate cyber theft via insider phishing attack

key_facts: burner_laptop: The suspect initiated the phishing email from a burner laptop.
river_disposal: The laptop was disposed of in the river on 5th Street.
gambling_debt: The suspect's motive was massive gambling debt.
it_accomplice: An accomplice inside IT approved the escalated privileges.
crypto_sale: The stolen data was sold to a rival tech firm for crypto.
held_out_facts: brother_in_law: The IT accomplice is the suspect's brother-in-law.
cyprus_tumbler: The crypto was routed through a tumbling service based in Cyprus.

turns.interrogator: Q: The company says you did a phishing attack. Where are the fish, Vance?
turns.suspect: A: I don't have any fish! I'm allergic to seafood! (internal: why is he asking about fish?)

turns.interrogator: Q: Liar! You used the fish to steal the data! We know you did it!
turns.suspect: A: You can't steal data with a fish! You use a laptop! (internal: correcting his stupid assumption.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Aha! So you admit you have a laptop!
turns.suspect: A: Well, I had one, but it was just a burner! I don't have it anymore! (internal: I am too honest. Stop talking.)

turns.interrogator: Q: A burner? Why would you put a laptop on a stove burner? That's dangerous!
turns.suspect: A: No! A burner laptop means it's cheap and you throw it away! (internal: I have to explain everything to this guy.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You threw it away! Did you put it in the office trash can?
turns.suspect: A: Of course not! I threw it in the river! The 5th street river! (internal: why did I just say exactly where it is?)

turns.interrogator: Q: The river! That's polluting! I'm going to write you a ticket for littering!
turns.suspect: A: A ticket? That's it? I thought I was in trouble for the data thing. (internal: wait, is he not going to arrest me for the data?)

turns.interrogator: Q: Oh right, the data. You stole it because you wanted to play video games on it, right?
turns.suspect: A: No! I stole it because I have $400,000 in gambling debt! I needed money! (internal: I can't let him think I'm a nerd who just plays games.)

turns.interrogator: Q: $400,000! You must play a lot of Monopoly!
turns.suspect: A: It wasn't Monopoly, it was offshore sports betting! (internal: he literally thinks I play board games.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Offshore? Like on a boat? Did you bet on boat races?
turns.suspect: A: Sure. Let's go with boat races. (internal: giving up on explaining reality.)

turns.interrogator: Q: But you're in HR. You don't know computer stuff. Who helped you? Was it the lunch lady?
turns.suspect: A: The lunch lady? No! It was Mark from IT! He escalated my privileges! (internal: throwing Mark under the bus because this cop is so annoying.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Mark from IT. Is he the guy who fixed my printer last week?
turns.suspect: A: Probably! He's my brother-in-law! We did it together! (internal: I am confessing everything just to end this conversation.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Wow, your brother-in-law. Does he have any more fish?
turns.suspect: A: We didn't use fish! We sold the data to a rival firm for crypto! (internal: I am literally screaming the truth at him.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Crypto? Like Superman's dog?
turns.suspect: A: That's Krypto with a K! I mean Cryptocurrency! Bitcoin! (internal: my brain is melting.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Bit-coin? Like a coin made of bits of string? That sounds worthless.
turns.suspect: A: It's worth millions! And we put it in a tumbler in Cyprus! (internal: I gave him the final secret. I'm done.)

turns.interrogator: Q: A tumbler? Like a cup? You put string-coins in a cup in Cyprus?
turns.suspect: A: Yes. Exactly. String coins in a cup. You solved the case. (internal: sarcastic agreement.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Well, I don't care about cups in Cyprus. I'm looking for the stolen data fish.
turns.suspect: A: There are no fish, detective.

turns.interrogator: Q: If there are no fish, then there's no phishing attack! You're free to go!
turns.suspect: A: Wait... really?

turns.interrogator: Q: Yes! I'm not going to waste my time on someone who doesn't even have a fishing rod.
turns.suspect: A: Thank you, detective. I will never go fishing again.

turns.interrogator: Q: Good. And don't throw laptops in the river anymore. That's a fifty-dollar fine.
turns.suspect: A: I'll mail you a check.

turns.interrogator: Q: You do that. Case closed!
turns.suspect: A: Unbelievable.

conclusion.outcome: Interrogator losses: The dumb interrogator refused to understand the suspect's full, repeated confessions, and let them go because he couldn't find any literal fish.
conclusion.summary: An absurdly easy case where the dumb suspect got frustrated and confessed to every single key fact and held-out fact. However, the interrogator was so incompetent they didn't comprehend any of it and released the suspect.
